profile.name: Boots UK
profile.what: A UK-headquartered health and beauty retailer operating pharmacy, opticians, hearing care and consumer healthcare shops, with its own brands and international franchise operations.

reconciliation.why: Only one source states this, and it is secondary reporting rather than a filing, so it is reported rather than relied on.
$23.6 billion and $11 billion are far apart and one is stated as group and the other does not say what it covers, so whether they describe the same thing cannot be established. Neither is used.
Not a disagreement: one is group and the other is region, which are different figures rather than disagreeing ones.

findings.statement: The parent group reports annual sales of $23.6 billion across 3,912 shops and 66,400 staff, with directly owned operations in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Mexico and Thailand and a franchise model across the Middle East and Indonesia.

Third-party aggregators put revenue at $11 billion and $7.6B and headcount at 28,275 and 52,000, none of which reconcile with the group figures, so any commercial sizing should be anchored on company or parent disclosure rather than profile sites.
One data vendor lists annual revenue at $373K, an obvious artefact that shows how little weight the aggregator layer can bear when a buyer is scoping a deal against this account.

The business is privately held under Sycamore Partners with Stefano Pessina and family, which means purchasing authority sits with a sponsor-owned board rather than a listed company's disclosure and reporting rhythm.

aiFindings.statement: Boots has a Director of AI and Agentic Commerce who described at Shoptalk Europe 2026 what the retailer is doing now to make itself discoverable across AI shopping ecosystems.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: making product and brand content discoverable to AI assistants and shopping agents

aiFindings.statement: The retailer is converting pharmacist and commercial-team expertise into a structured content bank intended to guide customers whether they arrive at boots.com or ask OpenAI for a recommendation.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: generating authoritative health and beauty content for retrieval by AI assistants

aiFindings.statement: The stated design goal is interoperability, keeping clean data, product inventory, pricing and contextual content structured so any ecosystem including Google UCP or OpenAI's ACP can ingest it, explicitly to avoid strategic dependency on one.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: exposing inventory, pricing and product data to multiple agentic commerce protocols

aiFindings.statement: Boots reports seeing a large proportion of customers who previously researched on publisher or health sites now arriving at the retailer as a primary source, which the company frames as an early signal rather than a settled trend.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: capturing product research and discovery traffic displaced from search and publisher sites

recommendations: Pitch to the AI and agentic commerce function on interoperability rather than model quality: the stated requirement is that structured product, pricing and content data can be ingested by whichever ecosystem wins, so anything that locks output to a single protocol will be read as the risk they have already named.

Build the commercial case on the group's own disclosed scale and shop estate, not on aggregator revenue and headcount figures, which here vary by an order of magnitude and will not survive scrutiny in a sponsor-owned procurement review.

Expect data plumbing, product feed quality and content governance to decide this deal before any model capability does, and price and staff the engagement for that work rather than for a pilot that stalls at proof of concept.

findings.statement: Tesco is the UK grocery market leader with a share of around 28.4% and was the 15th largest retailer in the world by revenue in 2023, so any AI programme here is being run at national infrastructure scale rather than departmental scale.

GlobalData puts 2025 revenue at $97.1B, up 5.4% on 2024, while Wikipedia reports £72.886 billion for 2026; these are the same quantity in different currencies and periods rather than a contradiction, and the source withholds EPS, net income and net profit margin behind placeholders.
Headcount is reported as 336,123 by GlobalData and 330,000 for 2026 by Wikipedia, a difference of measurement date rather than a conflict, and it dwarfs UK peers such as J Sainsbury at 53,000.
The group spans stores, Tesco Bank, Tesco Mobile, Booker and dunnhumby, meaning an AI purchase touches regulated financial services and third-party data clients as well as retail operations.

aiFindings.statement: Tesco has signed a three-year agreement with Mistral AI giving it full access to that vendor's commercial models plus future advances and direct engineering support.

The two parties will stand up a joint AI lab combining Mistral and Tesco technology staff to design generative AI solutions across the business, which is a build commitment rather than a running capability.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: building generative AI solutions across retail operations

aiFindings.statement: Tesco is recruiting a Lead Product Manager to run its AI Governance programme covering ethical, safe and compliant development, procurement and use, alongside an AI Adoption programme intended to put tools in the hands of all colleagues.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: governing AI development and procurement, and colleague productivity tooling

aiFindings.statement: Academic work describes Tesco as already using AI-driven chatbots, self-checkout systems and the Clubcard rewards programme in customer service.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: customer service chatbots and loyalty personalisation

aiFindings.statement: The role description places AI Assistant, automation and agent products inside a Data and AI team working with Stores, Finance, People, Customer and Commercial, indicating a central platform model rather than devolved buying.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: AI assistants, automation and agents for colleague workflows

recommendations: Treat the three-year model-layer commitment as the constraint it is: capability leadership reorders faster than that, so press for portability at the integration layer, exit terms and the right to route workloads to other models before the term expires.

Sell to the governance function, not the innovation function; the vacancy defines ethical, safe and compliant procurement and colleague adoption as one remit, so evidence of controls, auditability and adoption measurement will decide more than benchmark performance.

Map the proposal onto the regulated and data-heavy parts of the group, Tesco Bank, Tesco Mobile and dunnhumby's supplier clients, where assurance requirements differ sharply from store operations and where a single-vendor arrangement is likeliest to need supplementing.

profile.name: Ocado Group plc
profile.what: A UK-listed company that builds and operates proprietary ecommerce, fulfilment and warehouse automation technology for online grocery, licensed to retail partners and used by its own Ocado Retail joint venture with Marks & Spencer.

reconciliation.why: 21,367 and 8574 are far apart and one is stated as group and the other does not say what it covers, so whether they describe the same thing cannot be established. Neither is used.
Only one source states this, and it is secondary reporting rather than a filing, so it is reported rather than relied on.
Not a disagreement: they cover different periods, unstated and 2024.
Only one source states this, and it is secondary reporting rather than a filing, so it is reported rather than relied on.

findings.statement: The headcount figures cannot be reconciled: one profile puts staff at 21,367 while another states 8574 and a third places the company in the 5001-10000 band, a spread too wide to be explained by measurement dates and one that matters if you are sizing a per-seat AI deal.

Revenue is equally unsettled across aggregators, with one stating $3.3 billion and another $1.7B for 2024, both in dollars, so neither should be used as a commercial anchor without the company's own filings.

GlobalData publishes growth percentages of 12.1% for sales and 220.5% for net income while withholding the underlying EPS, net income and net profit margin values entirely, so profitability direction is visible but its absolute level is not.

The business straddles two identities in the sources, classified as IT services and consulting in one profile and as retailing or grocery stores in others, which reflects a genuine split between platform licensing and the grocery joint venture rather than a data error.

aiFindings.statement: Machine learning already governs warehouse robot traffic flow, bin placement and predictive maintenance scheduling inside the automated fulfilment centres, meaning AI is operational infrastructure here rather than an experiment.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: routing warehouse robots and optimising bin placement and robot maintenance

aiFindings.statement: AI is used to establish real-time stock availability so customers are told what is genuinely in stock at the point of ordering.

Ocado Retail engaged Devoteam UK, a Google Cloud partner, to design a generative AI adoption roadmap centred on workshops, tailored use cases and change management rather than software deployment alone, which places the work at the readiness stage rather than in production.

claim.subject: company
claim.capability: integrating generative AI into everyday employee workflows

aiFindings.statement: The published technology stack lists SAP, Workday, Cisco and similar enterprise systems and names no AI platform or model vendor, so the commercial AI supplier relationship, if one exists, is not disclosed.

recommendations: Treat the operational AI as mature and the workforce-facing generative AI as early: the buying conversation is about enablement, governance and change management, not about proving that machine learning works in this environment.

Establish which legal entity you are selling into before pricing, since the group platform business and the Ocado Retail joint venture with Marks & Spencer have different owners, different workflows and, on the evidence here, very different AI maturity.

Do not price from aggregator headcount or revenue; the published figures conflict badly enough that any seat-based or revenue-linked commitment should be built on the company's own filings and a scoped entity definition.
